scope: Changed applications only; extend the preserved Version15 inventory without relabeling historical approvals.

applications.source: Internal horizontal Taylor homomorphism, Taylor criterion B.9 and product rule B.4; prior normalization in the later linearization proof.
applications.required: Exact vector-space horizontal Taylor identities for chosen real lifts before dividing by M into a smaller horizontal lattice.
applications.constructed: Right multiplication by the fixed-order product of gamma_(h,i)^(-binomial(n,i)), gamma in the internal lattice intersected with G_(i,1).
applications.domain_coverage: For each finitely many weights i, the existing modulo-lattice identity says the difference lies in the image of Gamma intersect G_(i,1); choose an internal preimage.
applications.maps: Right multiplication leaves g_h Gamma unchanged. Horizontal Taylor is additive and removes precisely the i-th difference. After removal, x/M paired with M phi(e) preserves the vector identity.
applications.conventions: Horizontal quotient G_(i,1)/G_(i,2) is additive; chosen real lifts rather than arbitrary torus roots; fixed product order, no commutativity assumed.
applications.exceptions: Rational and small coordinate removals use the fixed rational/small lifts. Linear petals use {alpha h} beta. Core and independent roots must agree with lift division.
applications.uniformity: Finite weights; internal choices. Standard finite covering and denominator frozen on the dense internal subfamily as before.
applications.consumer: Representation on the covering lattice Gamma prime and subsequent independent-frequency/coset analysis.
applications.change: Omitted justification at this location; prior device exists later. The quartic data and asserted theorem statements do not change.

applications.source: Gaudron–Rémond, Théorème des périodes et degrés minimaux d’isogénies, Comment. Math. Helv.89(2014),343–403, DOI10.4171/CMH/322, Section2.3 and Corollary8.4.
applications.required: Stable Faltings-height lower bound and the upper height change under an isogeny of degree D.
applications.constructed: Abelian varieties E,B,A over the indicated number fields in the existing isogeny-factor proof.
applications.domain_coverage: Number-field abelian varieties; stable height can be computed after a semistable extension.
applications.maps: B to A isogeny of degree D; retain direction and one-half logarithmic term.
applications.conventions: Use the manuscript stable-height normalization; source Section2.3 distinguishes height normalizations. Do not import an unstable height or reverse the inequality.
applications.exceptions: Dimension-zero height separately set to zero. Positive-dimensional E uses the printed lower bound.
applications.uniformity: No new effective constant or theorem application is added; identify the actual source of the two existing inequalities.
applications.consumer: Height bound for the abelian surface factor and the five-contact estimate.
applications.change: Bibliography correction only. Preserve gr2014 Duke key for Theorem1.4/Section9 applications.

applications.source: Tao–Ziegler, published results cited by v5tz, Theorems9,11,13,15 and Corollary3; existing local adaptation in the manuscript.
applications.required: Dense-model and polynomial-average estimates with W=E product_(p<=v)p for fixed E.
applications.constructed: Same functions and same non-squarefree W as Version15; no replacement theorem or proof route.
applications.domain_coverage: Unit residues; v ultimately contains all prime divisors of fixed D and E.
applications.maps: Fixed extra modulus factor in the divisor-sum construction. Theorem9 is a bounded-function statement independent of W.
applications.conventions: Published statements use the squarefree primorial. Mark the non-squarefree use as a proof adaptation, not a direct statement application.
applications.exceptions: Small-prime divisibility excluded by unit residues; other prime factors treated by existing divisor-sum estimates.
applications.uniformity: E fixed before the asymptotic limit; polynomial coefficient bounds absorb fixed E.
applications.consumer: Fixed Artin conditions in quadratic patterns.
applications.change: Scope clarification only. Fable followed but did not re-derive every modified-modulus estimate; the alternative statement-only route is not inserted.
